techniques.evidence: crates/api/src/judges.rs:88 The three-state verdict is computed and attached, but untrusted/unknown only blocks when the project opts in. The standard says these states never fail a release, so this should be the default and not an opt-in.

crates/api/src/labels.rs:80 create_label accepts a dataset_item subject with no frozen-dataset check (neither store's insert_label checks either). The human ground truth of a frozen golden set can therefore change without a version bump, although item writes are refused (datasets.rs:102).

crates/api/src/benchmarks.rs:387 Covers the 'no merged series / identity on every verdict' rule only: a run pinned to a different judge is refused comparison against the stored baseline. No published-benchmark replay exists, and none is needed here.

pairs.subject: judge-calibration-and-drift
pairs.evidence: crates/runner/src/calibrate_watch.rs:81 The sentinel warns on any per-cycle kappa drop larger than a fixed drift_threshold (default 0.15), and nothing measures the judge's per-dimension repeatability floor beneath it. Re-score noise can therefore page on a cadence.

techniques.evidence: crates/runner/src/calibrate_watch.rs:81 Drift is a configured delta with no measured floor. A repo grep for repeatab/flip_rate found only the batch-method flip count, and no N-times identical re-score exists.

crates/runner/src/calibrate_watch.rs:30 Realized: daemon and --once modes, the previous kappa read before re-judging, persistence, a below-bar alert plus a sharp-drop warning on stderr, and a reserved exit code. Edge case: a cycle where every item fails to parse yields n=0, kappa 0, and exits 5, so a pipeline fault reads as untrusted.

crates/runner/src/calibration_post.rs:41 The record names the dataset but never sets dataset_version, and load_set (calibrate.rs:54) does not require a frozen set, so kappa history cannot tell a judge change from a golden-set change. The metric family, the judge-only design and skipped-item handling are realized.

crates/runner/src/calibration_post.rs:82 The derived lt:calibration score carries the product rubric_id. Score::alert_key keys on that id, so the kappa series shares a score_drop window with that rubric's product scores and with every other judge calibrated on it.

crates/runner/src/calibrate.rs:276 Within this context: a pre-set kappa bar (CLI default 0.6), an explicit verdict, and the verdict persisted on the record and score. How the gates consume it is judged under evaluation-pipeline.

crates/runner/src/calibrate.rs:248 Calibration folds into kappa, pearson, MAE, RMSE and bias, with no known-good vs known-bad spread column and no multi-judge bake-off. The method-change re-verification half is realized: calibrate_batch.rs:299 does a paired batch-vs-single comparison with pass/fail flips.

pairs.registryProposal: reserved-rubric-persistence assumes the reserved rubric NAME is the alert series key. In a store that types scores and keys windows on a rubric id, attaching the product rubric id to a calibration probe silently merges the kappa series with product quality. The technique should state that the reserved namespace must be the series key, not just the label.

techniques.evidence: crates/store-pg/src/calibrations.rs:64 Scope is judge+rubric only. dataset_version is stored but ignored by latest(), and the threshold is not persisted (COLS has kappa_bar only).

crates/store-pg/src/calibrations.rs:22 Calibration history is append-only (insert/latest/list, no update or delete), so a recalibration never restates an earlier cycle. The alert-series keying problem lives in core and the runner, not here.
